title: Crescent watch cribsheet: quick handover & temporary ops
content:
Purpose / TL;DR:
Quick scribble for the 00:00–08:00 crescent watch. Not polished — meant for whoever picks this up: what I saw, what I did, what still needs follow-up. Use at-will, update live.

Status snapshot (as I leave):
- Platform: GREEN. No P0s open.
- Recent flares: short-lived token cache thrash (approx 00:40–01:05) causing 503s to the hosted-api route /v1/generate with long prompts (>6k tokens).
- Impact: ~12 requests retried by clients; default retry policy absorbed most. No customer SLAs breached per console alerts.
- Current load: steady at ~60% burst capacity on dedicated pool east-1; autoscale is healthy.

What I did (chronological):
- 00:42: noticed spike in error rate on alerts (observability > per-route errors).
- Checked logs: pattern = KV cache miss + concurrent cold-start on the shard.
- Quick mitigation: temporarily bumped per-shard warmup setting for model-llama-70b-q4 -> changed from 30s to 90s (console: Models -> model-llama-70b-q4 -> config -> warmup-seconds).
- Deployed a short-lived routing fallback: routed low-priority traffic to model-llama-70b-q4-quantized-compat for 10m (route: hosted-api/default, add fallback).
- Monitored: error rate dropped back to baseline by 01:00. Reverted fallback at 01:15.
- Left warmup at 90s because traces show spikes when warmup was 30s. Needs follow-up (see Questions).

Immediate checks for next shift (quick list):
- Observe per-route 5xx (console -> per-route -> last 6h). If >0.5% sustained for 15 minutes, escalate to SRE oncall.
- Check dedication pool utilization (Dedicated -> Pools -> east-1-crescent). If queued requests > 20 for 5m, run capacity-bump documented below.
- Look for KV cache thrash patterns: repeated kv-cache-miss on same request prefixes. If seen, suspect recent model rollout or kernel mismatch.

Temp procedures / quick run commands:
- Check API error timeline (kubectl logs): kubectl -n inference logs -l app=api-gateway --since=2h | grep "503" | tail -n 50
- Inspect serving node queues: rcli nodes list --region east-1 --format json | jq '.[] | {id, queued, healthy}'
- Bump warmup for model: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://console.redwood.ai/api/models/{model_id}/config -d '{"warmup_seconds":90}'
- Temporary route fallback (console quick): Console -> Routing -> select hosted-api -> Add fallback model (quantized compat) -> 10min -> save and monitor.

Escalation ladder (who to ping):
- Stage 1: Slack #sre-oncall and tag @oncall (for immediate noisy errors).
- Stage 2: Pager: Jonah Kim (primary), Priya Singh (secondary). Pager contacts in PagerDuty: JKim (primary), PSingh (secondary).
- Stage 3: If GPU host OOM or node crash affecting >2 shards -> page infra-lead (pager infra-lead).

Example Slack blurbs (copy/paste):
- Short alert share: "@sre-oncall seeing transient 503s on hosted-api /v1/generate (long prompt). Bumped model warmup to 90s and added temporary fallback to quantized compat. Error rate back to baseline. Investigating KV cache misses. @Jonah-Kim FYI."
- If escalating: "Paging oncall: sustained 5xx >0.5% for 20m on hosted-api -> escalating to SRE primary. Links: <INF-2187>"

Open follow-ups / questions (to assign):
- Why did warmup=30s cause thrash in the early hours but not earlier in the day? Hypothesis: shift in token-length distribution from batch jobs that kick in at 00:30. Need trace correlation with batch jobs. (Assign to Priya)
- Can we add a temporary throttle in the batch ingestion pipeline between 00:20–01:10 to smooth sequence-length spikes? (Product question — link to INF-2187)
- Confirm that the quantized fallback has identical safety hooks (it does, but need verification from model-onboarding team).

Misc notes / evidence:
- Link to trace of incident: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/trace-9a3b (saved snapshot at 00:45).
- Logs gist: https://paste.redwood.ai/r/nbv2 (contains grep output used above).
- Key errors seen: "kv-cache-miss", "serve-shard-cold-start", "model-kernel-mismatch: warn".

Checklist for next shift lead to finalize and close: 
- Re-evaluate warmup setting in morning (08:00 local) after traffic pattern settles -> if stable, revert to 45s and monitor for 2h.
- Create a short perf-eval ticket to correlate tokenizer/profile with batch jobs (INF followup assigned).
- Add a Playbook snippet (temp) under Confluence section "Serving runtime -> Warmup heuristics" (I left a draft in the linked INF ticket).

Quick wins and heuristics (lessons learned):
- If you see kv-cache-miss spikes clustered, think warmup+cold-start, not model degradation. Rapid fallback to quantized variant usually buys time.
- Avoid flipping too many knobs at once — change one parameter, watch 15m.

Random notes to self (not urgent):
- Probe idea: add a short-running synthetic long-prompt generator around 23:50 to prime KV caches for midnight batch. Might reduce cold-start window.
- Confirm whether autoscaling has per-shard min replicas set; if not, propose a min=1 for high-latency models.

If you take this shift, leave an update at top (timestamp + short lines). I try to be concise — if you need more context ping me directly in DMs.

— Ava M.
